title: Ahdc1 loss selectively depresses neuronal surface and synaptic transcripts in 151 TH without canonical Wnt activation
exact_observed_result: Ahdc1 perturbation produced an FDR-supported response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, dominated by decreases in Ptprz1, Spock3, Lrp1b, Tro, Gria2, Cdh18, Ache, Calb1, and Wls without Axin2 or Nkd1 induction.
biological_interpretation: AHDC1 loss in the assayed thalamic neurons is better framed as neuronal surface/synaptic transcript loss than as an APC-like Wnt activation state.

evidence_records.statistics: 243 perturbed cells versus 23679 controls; 17259 genes tested; 13 genes at FDR<0.05 and 17 at FDR<0.10; minimum FDR=2.004e-05.
evidence_records.description: Ahdc1 produced its only FDR-significant differentially expressed gene set in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class.

evidence_records.statistics: Across the 21 non-151 cell-type contrasts, 0 genes reached FDR<0.05 or FDR<0.10; the next-best minimum FDR values were 0.113 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 0.124 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 0.169 in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 0.212 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
evidence_records.description: The FDR-corrected Ahdc1 response was absent outside 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

evidence_records.statistics: 155 MB Glut had 245 perturbed cells versus 20353 controls, no genes at FDR<0.05, minimum FDR=0.668, and Ahdc1 logFC -0.056 with FDR=1.000; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut had 157 perturbed cells, no FDR<0.05 genes, and Ahdc1 logFC +0.034 with FDR=1.000.
evidence_records.description: At least two reasonably powered Ahdc1 contrasts had almost no FDR-corrected transcriptomic response.

caveats: The story is grounded in one corrected cell type and does not establish that AHDC1 acts through the same pathway in other neuronal populations.

prior_expectation.summary: Prior literature and pathway context were taken from the resolved report references; the observed Perturb-seq signal either refines expected gene function by cell type or marks an exploratory response-state neighbor where noted in caveats.

citations.citation: Xia F et al. De novo truncating mutations in AHDC1 in individuals with syndromic expressive language delay, hypotonia, and sleep apnea. Am J Hum Genet. 2014;94(5):784-789.
citations.supports: Original report linking de novo AHDC1 truncating variants to a syndrome with developmental delay, hypotonia, intellectual disability, and sleep apnea.

citations.citation: Human Protein Atlas AHDC1 gene entry ENSG00000126705.
citations.supports: Human expression database entry annotating AHDC1 as detected across brain regions with low brain regional specificity.
